before_step.derivation: Given step 1: initial setup s0(J)=idx(J) mod 3; transition setup s(I,J)=abs(idx(I)-idx(J)) mod 3 for distinct consecutive jobs I,J. Fix a sequence J1,...,Jn (a permutation of A-H). Machine is nonpreemptive and single; setup for a job may begin only after that job's release r(J) and after the prior job completes. Let C0=0. For k=1: the machine is idle until setup can begin at t=max(C0, r(J1))=r(J1) (since r>=0); setup runs s0(J1); then processing p(J1) runs. So setup start SS1=r(J1), processing start PS1=SS1+s0(J1), completion C1=PS1+p(J1). For k>=2: setup for Jk begins only after Jk's release and after prior completion C(k-1), i.e. SSk=max(C(k-1), r(Jk)); PSk=SSk+s(I,Jk) where I=J(k-1); Ck=PSk+p(Jk). This is well defined for any sequence; no objective or comparison is introduced here. Note releases are given per job, and setup/processing are sequential with no overlap.
before_step.result: For sequence J1..Jn: SS1=r(J1), PS1=r(J1)+s0(J1), C1=PS1+p(J1). For k>=2: SSk=max(C(k-1), r(Jk)), PSk=SSk+s(J(k-1),Jk), Ck=PSk+p(Jk). Well defined for any fixed sequence.

plan_step.goal: For a fixed sequence, define setup start, processing start, and completion using release dates, setup times, and nonpreemptive machine constraints.

returned_step.derivation: Fix any permutation J1,...,Jn of the eight jobs. Let C0=0 denote machine availability before the first job. Setup cannot begin before the job's release nor before the prior job has completed, and processing cannot overlap setup or another job. For k=1, SS1=max(C0,r(J1))=r(J1), since every release is nonnegative. The initial setup then runs for s0(J1), so PS1=SS1+s0(J1), and processing runs for p(J1), so C1=PS1+p(J1). For k>=2, let I=J(k-1). Setup for Jk begins only after both the previous completion and Jk's release, hence SSk=max(C(k-1),r(Jk)). Then PSk=SSk+s(I,Jk), where s(I,Jk)=abs(idx(I)-idx(Jk)) mod 3 is the between-job setup from step 1. Completion is Ck=PSk+p(Jk). Because SSk>=C(k-1), this setup-plus-processing interval starts after the prior job completes and, once started, is nonpreemptive: setup immediately precedes processing with no interruption. This recursively defines all setup starts, processing starts, and completions for any fixed sequence; no objective or optimization is introduced.
